# v9 post-hoc addendum results (generated by `scripts/summarize_v9_addendum.py`)

**Exploratory, written after the preregistered runs.** Nothing here changes a preregistered verdict (those are in `docs/v9_results.md`). Why these analyses exist: `docs/v9_review.md`.

## 1. Exact reproduction and robustness of the preregistered tests

The addendum recomputes the same splits from scratch (with a fresh cshrink cache) and keeps per-entry errors with coordinates. Reproduction = max |RMSE difference| vs the frozen run over all frozen methods.

| Holdout | reproduction (MCAR / MNAR) | H16 entry / protein-cluster / per-split t | H17 | H18 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| derks2022 | 0.0e+00 / 0.0e+00 | 12/20 / 12/20 / 12/20 (strict: 12/20 / 12/20 / 12/20) | 4/4 / 4/4 / 4/4 (strict: 2/4 / 2/4 / 2/4) | 11/12 / 11/12 / 10/12 (strict: 8/12 / 8/12 / 8/12) |

## 2. Added comparators on the holdouts: RMSE relative to the champion

`bpca_oba` = correctly oriented BPCA (proteins as observations, as in pcaMethods/MSnbase); the frozen panel's `bpca` was effectively mean imputation. PIMMS = Webel et al. 2024 (pimms-learn 0.5.2).

## 3. Counterfactual: the preregistered tests with a working BPCA as the data-only comparator

On dev, `bpca_oba+stack` (0.9914 x champion) would have narrowly displaced `gcn_nograph+stack` (0.9917) under the frozen selection rule. Below: champion and revised vs `bpca_oba+stack` (and raw `bpca_oba`), entry bootstrap, preregistered pass rule (CI < 0 and <= -1%). Negative = our method is better.

| Holdout | mask | champion vs bpca_oba+stack (all / in-cx) | revised vs bpca_oba+stack (all / in-cx) |
|---|---|---|---|
| derks2022 | MCAR | +2.23% ✗ / +2.02% ✗ | +0.97% ✗ / +0.89% ✗ |
| derks2022 | MNAR | +3.28% ✗ / +3.73% ✗ | +0.15% ✗ / +0.82% ✗ |
